subject: clockworkDog
pitch: A wind-up clockwork terrier made of polished brass and copper. Riveted body plates, visible gears turning in its chest, a big winding key on its back, springy jointed legs, floppy leather ears, glass-lens eyes with a green tint, a tail made of a coiled spring, and a little red collar with a brass tag.
reasoning:
I'm planning a terrier model standing about 0.45m tall, built from a hip-rooted skeleton with spine, neck, head, jaw, ears, tail, and four legs, keeping the SDK calls limited to joints, chains, parts, sweeps, spikes, and extrusions for efficiency.

Now I'm working out joint placement for the body - hips, chest, spine chain with catmull curves, and legs using a limb helper that generates hip/knee/foot points with appropriate bend directions for front versus hind legs, then connecting the neck and head joints off the spine chain's endpoint.

I'm figuring out how to render the torso itself, considering a sweep along the spine path with a box-like or octagon cross-section bound to the spine bones for a simple rigid body shape.

For the surface detail, I'm planning riveted copper panels on the sides with small sphere rivets attached to the first spine bone, plus a chest feature with dark porthole-style discs on either side to show the gears underneath.

Rather than true transparent glass, I'll fake the gear window using layered cylinders—a geared disc with a darker inner hub, oriented so its flat face points outward, framed by a brass torus bezel. Then I'm adding a winding key on the back, starting a stem rod from the upper back point.

Designing butterfly handle outline...

Then I'm moving to the head shape, using a frustum box for the skull, positioned forward and slightly above the spine, tapering in width and height.

Still shaping the ear geometry...

Now I'm working out leg placement: front legs with shoulder-to-foot points and lengths, and hind legs with hip-knee-hock-foot chains, checking reach distances stay plausible and naming each segment accordingly.

I also want to add springy coil details on the lower legs, wrapping a spiral sweep around the shin segment with a few turns and a small radius to suggest a spring, positioning the coil's center and axis along the leg line.

Still building leg geometry...

For the legs I'm setting up the chain naming and parenting - front legs attach to the spine, hind legs attach to hips, with joint names like fhip/fknee/fankle per side. Then I'm designing the tail as a curved spring-like chain starting near the hips, using a catmull path that arcs upward and back with tail1/tail2 segments, considering whether to coil it along the path for a springy look.

Now I'm working out the collar piece — a closed ring swept around the neck joint using catmull points, sizing the radius so it sits just outside the neck geometry, anchored at the midpoint of the neck chain.

For the tag, I'm picking the bottom-front ring item (roughly the middle index) and attaching a small brass disc stick there, oriented outward along the item's facing axis so it hangs naturally against the neck. I'm skipping extra details like decals or text for now to keep things simple.

Now I'm moving on to the neck chain, building it from two joints curving up from the spine toward the head position, then defining the head joint itself. For the head bone, I'm adding a brass skull box and a tapered muzzle frustum extending forward, and I'm about to set up the jaw joint next.

Adding brows and ears now, with a catmull-rom sweep for ear shape using leather color, parented to the head. I'm setting side conventions so s=1 is left (+X) and s=-1 is right, naming the ear meshes accordingly.

Now I'm placing copper rivet plates along the back spine of the body, positioning a small box plate near the top of the torso where the body radius narrows, checking the y-coordinate against the body path heights to get it sitting flush around 0.478.

Then I'm adding flank plates on the sides of the body around the hip area, and gear-like portholes on the chest at x=±0.112, accounting for the octagonal cross-section of the body (vertices falling on both top and side positions since 8 is divisible by 4) so the flat faces sit at the correct cosine-adjusted offset, settling the plate center at x=0.103.

Now I'm designing the porthole bezels as torus rings with a dark backing disc behind them, then building two nested gear discs inside each porthole using faceted low-segment cylinders to fake teeth, with a smaller inner ring and hub for depth.

Attaching the gears to the spine1/spine bone near the chest, then working out rivet placements around the back and side plates — using merged sphere geometries per color for the brass rivets, positioned at the plate corners and edges to avoid clipping.

I'm also adding a belly panel, chest plate, shoulder bolt, tail ring, and hip plate, plus setting up the full color palette (brass, copper, dark, green, leather, red, steel) kept flat without extra shading. Checking overall proportions now — head top around 0.67, key handle reaching up to 0.69 — to make sure everything fits together properly before exporting.

Now I'm defining the key joint off the spine, building a brass stem rod up to the handle with a copper extrusion and a small spinning base disc, then moving on to writing the leg limb code that returns chained position arrays for each leg.

For the spring, I'm computing a helical coil wrapped around the lower leg segment, deriving the axis from the vector between the two leg points, offsetting the starting point perpendicular to that axis, and setting the coil's length, turns, and pitch so it wraps naturally along the limb.

I'll keep the coil radius constant, give the hind leg two simple segments without a separate hock joint, and skip detailed teeth geometry. For the body and neck I'm building tapered sweeps with polygonal cross-sections, adding a collar ring positioned at the neck's midpoint.
